question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-1)({e}^{y}-1)}{x{e}^{y}}, & x\ge 1,\,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $x\ge 1,\,y\ge 0.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y).
$$

For $x\ge 1$ and $y\ge 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{(x-1)({e}^{y}-1)}{x{e}^{y}})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x-1}{x}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(1-\frac{1}{{e}^{y}})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x-1}{x}\cdot \frac{1}{{e}^{y}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{y}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(1-\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{y}}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}{e}^{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Otherwise, $f(x,y)=0.$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}{e}^{y}}, & x\ge 1,\,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
